The preserve of hard workers for the best part of two centuries, the chore jacket is one of those garments that brings with it a reassuring sense of solidity.
We took our popular Five-Pocket Chore Jacket (so called because it is a counterpart to our Five-Pocket Trousers, not, as you may think, because of the number of pockets it has – it actually has six pockets) and had it made up in that most revered of working fabrics.
Crafted from a robust 12.6oz cotton duck, a tightly woven cotton fabric with two yarns in the warp and a single yarn in the weft for a smooth, plain weave less prone to tears, the name is derived from from the dutch word for cotton - ‘doek’ - and since 1899 has been used for sails, tents and, of course, workwear.
In doing so, we have created a piece of clothing with all the utility of a chore jacket – a surfeit of pockets; a comfortable, roomy shape – that will age and patinate beautifully over the years.
Finishing things off with classic copper rivets and you have an unbeatable everyday jacket, unmatched in its durability and timeless design. If you feel so inclined, you could even wear it to do your chores. It won’t let you down.

Though hopsack is traditionally associated with suiting, we’ve always admired how lighter versions translate beautifully into shirting, offering a refined hand, natural stretch, and a weave that instantly catches the eye. This season, we’ve taken things further with an all-new hopsack developed from a remarkable four-ply flat yarn, unlike anything we’ve used before.
Instead of twisting the yarns together, each of the four strands lies side by side, creating a fabric that’s flatter, softer, and more lustrous from the start. This structure also opens up the weave, giving it a subtle check-like pattern that feels both classic and modern. And because the flat yarns generate less friction as they interlace, the fabric naturally delivers an impressive diagonal stretch, all while being woven entirely from cotton.
The result is a hopsack that looks distinguished, feels luxurious, and performs with ease. It's a perfect foundation for your next custom shirt.

Introducing the Fat Fox Selvedge, a 22.7oz Japanese duck canvas made entirely from organic FoxFibre cotton, grown in California by cotton breeder and environmental pioneer Sally Fox. This fabric contains no dyes, bleach or chemical coloration. The warm brown color comes directly from the naturally pigmented cotton plant.

We're extremely excited about our iteration. We developed this discharge-printed moleskin, but it's not like our usual moleskin. It's also a much narrower, finer dotted-stripe printed than what you would normally seen on a Wabash stripe. This gives it more of a salt-and-pepper look at first glance.
